rules.title: Newark Rent Control – Surcharges and Hardship Increases
rules.requirement: Beyond the normal annual rent increase, a Newark landlord may seek extra rent through a tax surcharge (passing through increases in municipal property taxes), a capital/major-improvement surcharge, or a hardship increase (to earn a fair return), but each requires Rent Control Board approval, tenant notice, and the building must be in substantial compliance with codes.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rent-controlled dwellings registered under the Newark rent control ordinance; surcharges require Board petition, notice, and code-compliance inspection before approval.
rules.exemptions: No major-improvement surcharge may be granted if the dwelling is not in substantial compliance with codes or if registration requirements are not met; no increase allowed for improvements affecting more than 10 units unless total cost exceeds $2,000.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord may seek a tax surcharge from a tenant because of an increase in municipal property taxes. The tax surcharge shall not exceed that amount authorized by the following provision: The landlord shall divide one-twelfth (1/12th) of the annual increase in the present property tax over the property tax of the previous year by the total monthly rent roll, and that product shall be multiplied by the monthly rent paid by each tenant to establish the amount of surcharge that each tenant shall be required to pay.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the dwelling is in substantial compliance with building, fire, plumbing, electrical or housing codes and has met registration requirements

rules.conflict_note: This chunk covers only the surcharge/hardship-increase procedures of Newark's rent control ordinance; the base annual percentage cap itself is likely set out in a different section/chunk not included here.
